title: fix(cron): preserve pending reminder outcomes across restarts
body:
Related: #167796. Slice 1 of 4; the successor slices add controller-backed Automations execution and Claw review variants, migrate heartbeat declarations through Doctor, then remove retired heartbeat machinery and SDK exports. Each successor will start from the preceding landed result.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes main-session scheduled reminders being recorded as successful before a session adopts them, then silently disappearing when the Gateway restarts.

## User Impact

Pending reminders remain running until their exact queued occurrence is adopted. A restart before adoption records one interrupted error and removes that occurrence without replaying it. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The current Cron path treats a volatile queue insertion or heartbeat handoff as success ([original owner, lines 249–314](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/4587f83864cbe77329aea2c27b3cd2d2cbba18cb/src/cron/service/timer-execution.ts#L249-L314)). The existing system-event queue now reports exact-occurrence adoption separately from removal, and Cron retains its existing durable running receipt and cancellation handle until that result. Ordinary prompt admission and dedicated Cron heartbeat prompts acknowledge only their selected events; coalesced exec turns leave deferred reminders pending. Waiting for admission does not spend the execution watchdog.

This is the live-defect slice of the Peter-approved heartbeat-to-Automations work. The other slices preserve the approved design and public-surface decisions; they are deliberately absent here. Existing boolean/void Cron dependency adapters retain their existing contract; the built-in Gateway supplies the adoption receipt. This does not guarantee exactly-once external effects after adoption.

## Evidence

The new regression runs through CronService, persisted run history, the real event queue, and session prompt admission. Against unchanged production main `4587f83864cb`, both restart cases fail because history contains `ok`; the adoption-success case passes. On the candidate all three pass (1.1 seconds total case time). The five-file focused batch passes 83 cases: restart/adoption, watchdog, coalesced heartbeat event ownership, queue selection and capacity. The wrapper took 459 seconds, dominated by cold compilation and module loading; the existing heartbeat file accounts for most of that. Core types, corrected Cron test types, scoped typed lint, format and whitespace checks pass. Isolated Codex review is scoped-clean at P0–P2. After the adapter extraction, Gateway wiring and its shared-fixture stream lifecycle consumer pass all 111 cases (256 seconds wall time, including existing integration setup). Cold-start run recovery passes all 10 cases; the corrected restart/watchdog fixtures also pass their 13-case replay (120 seconds combined wall time). The final extracted version also passes the restart regression again (3/3; 66 seconds wall, mostly loading), core types, both affected test-type graphs and the line-growth ratchet; fresh Codex review is scoped-clean. The initial [CI run 39475320879](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39475320879) exposed two integration gaps, corrected in `3ae984477813`: legacy adapters must release cancellation at enqueue, and minimal Gateway fixtures need an actual session consumer before awaiting completed Cron runs. The existing cancellation assertion reproduced locally and remains unchanged. The corrected cancellation/restart/heartbeat cases pass 25/25; all four failed Gateway cases pass with a scoped wake consumer calling real prompt admission. Affected type graphs, typed lint, format, line-growth ratchet, and fresh independent review pass. The inline SDK review is fixed in `aef5560087b4`: adoption uses a core-only helper and the published consumption signature stays unchanged. The 69 queue/heartbeat ownership cases and all three restart cases pass again; core types, lint, line-growth and fresh scoped review pass. Current-head CI is [run 39480099033](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39480099033) on `aef5560087b41c256d7ab9fdad3dcaa5cb15be1d`. Its [compact-large-17 job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39480099033/job/118850673418) has one inherited failure: `get-reply-directives-apply.test.ts > keeps the active agent with independent policy=true` expects the removed `AgentSelectionRequiredError.surface` property. The exact selected test fails identically on clean CI main baseline `7e81872cbbc8992e887a22c79495a2583a7d5de3` (105.85 seconds) and on this candidate (41.37 seconds). The test, error class, directive owner, test config and lockfile inputs are byte-identical. Main independently corrects the stale assertion in [57689a77dc93](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/57689a77dc93f7ef55453faa75d7874aea3263f6), following the intentional private-field removal in #178545. This failure is outside S1; no assertions or budgets were weakened here. Attempt 2 is complete: this is the only failing test job, with its downstream aggregate gate. Five jobs stranded without runners in attempt 1 passed after the documented hosted failed-job retry; completed passing jobs were preserved. The automatic failure table has no corresponding main shard, so the exact-case baseline replay above supplies attribution. Native landing retains the red CI result under the authorized pre-existing-failure exception.

Team's October 12–15 journal shows restart exposure: 40 service stops and 22 KILL exits. Sanitized lines 975984, 976005–976201, 976387 and 976432–976437 show admission cleanup followed by sidecar waits and watchdog termination. This is exposure evidence, not a count of lost events. No live Gateway was modified.

The regression covers orderly restart cancellation and replacement; existing cold-start recovery tests cover abandoned durable runs. Real-provider end-to-end delivery is outside this slice's proof.

The test-graph boundary check reports existing oversized shards. A clean current-main control at `60cfa37acc6e` reports the identical counts: agents-tools 721, gateway-root 724, infra 723 and plugins-platform 727 against the 720 limit. No budget is changed. The new test belongs to services-cron, whose corrected types pass.

Change size: production +145/−50 (net +95), tests/support +298/−41 (net +257), docs +1. The production growth is the existing queue receipt and cancellation integration; it introduces no new durable owner. The Gateway adapter lives in the existing event-dispatch module, and both wiring fixtures share one queue mock factory; the two over-cap Gateway files shrink and the line-growth ratchet passes.
